jobs.title: Director of Membership (part-time)
jobs.excerpt: Who We AreAt Delve Deeper, we are a performance media agency specializing in the charity and nonprofit sector.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Delve Deeper, we are a performance media agency specializing in the charity and nonprofit sector. We partner with organizations that invest between $5 million and $20 million annually in media, helping mission-driven teams maximize their impact through advanced digital strategies that deliver measurable, scalable results.

Our capabilities span advanced reporting and analytics, intent-based audience segmentation, full-service digital media management, and personalized creative, providing our partners with a comprehensive, data-driven approach to growth.

Delve Deeper has been recognized as one of Built In Colorado’s “Best Places to Work” for five consecutive years, reflecting a culture that prioritizes both performance and people. We emphasize professional development and foster an environment where every team member can make a meaningful impact.

We are deeply committed to supporting our team members in their self-care, families, communities, and career growth. As a privately owned company, we move quickly, operate without unnecessary red tape, and create clear paths for advancement for those driven to succeed.

About The Giving Table

The Giving Table (TGT) brings together senior fundraising and marketing leaders from growth-minded nonprofits through thoughtfully curated peer groups. It offers C-suite leaders, Vice Presidents, and Directors a private space to bring their authentic selves to the table and openly discuss the personal and professional realities of nonprofit leadership.

Conversations may cover rising acquisition costs, board expectations, the impact of AI, donor lifetime value, attribution challenges, and the realities of leading through change. The topics vary, but the purpose remains the same: creating a trusted community where nonprofit leaders can learn from and support one another.

The Giving Table currently hosts gatherings in New York City, Washington, D.C., and Atlanta.

About the Role

We are looking for a relationship builder who fills the room and understands that the best business development often begins with trust, hospitality, and meaningful conversation.

As Director of Membership, you will own the full membership journey for The Giving Table. You will strengthen our prospect list, connect with the right leaders, extend thoughtful invitations, and determine who will be the best fit for each peer group.

Once members join, you will continue building those relationships, gradually moving each person from an initial introduction toward a broader commercial conversation with Delve Deeper when the timing is right.

You may be a Business Development Representative with a hospitality background or an events leader who has always understood that the real work is building relationships and generating revenue. Either way, you know how to make senior leaders feel welcome while maintaining a clear focus on growth and results.

You will report to the leader of The Giving Table and work closely with Delve Deeper’s marketing and client services teams.

What You Will Do

  • Build and maintain a highly targeted prospect list of Chief Development Officers, Chief Marketing Officers, Vice Presidents of Fundraising, Vice Presidents of Marketing, and other senior leaders at midsize and large nonprofits across the United States.
  • Grow membership in The Giving Table’s current markets, including New York City, Washington, D.C., and Atlanta.
  • Develop thoughtful, personalized outreach that reflects a genuine understanding of each prospect and their organization.
  • Leverage warm introductions, trusted industry relationships, and consistent follow-up to engage prospective members.
  • Curate peer groups of approximately seven to ten members, ensuring the right mix of organizations, cause areas, perspectives, and leadership experiences without placing direct competitors at the same table.
  • Own the member experience from initial invitation through attendance, including outreach, confirmations, restaurant selection, menu coordination, and other event logistics.
  • Attend select Giving Table dinners and events as a representative of Delve Deeper, strengthening relationships with members and ensuring a thoughtful, high-touch experience.
  • Work closely with our support team to manage invitations and RSVPs, keep prospect and member information current in HubSpot, and provide weekly pipeline reports.
  • Collaborate with internal hosts and facilitators to coordinate dinners, half-day sessions, off-sites, and salon-style conversations.
  • Work toward quarterly goals related to accepted members, event attendance, and membership growth.
  • Build referral networks by creating an experience members genuinely want to share with other leaders in their communities.
  • Develop relationships with the consultants, agencies, associations, and platform partners that serve the nonprofit fundraising community.
  • Identify opportunities to introduce engaged members to Delve Deeper’s client services team when the timing and need are right, without forcing the conversation.

Who You Are

  • You have at least three years of experience organizing high-touch development or relationship-building events for nonprofits, such as donor cultivation dinners, galas, advisory councils, major-gift roundtables, or capital campaign events. Comparable experience involving senior leaders in small, premium settings will also be considered.
  • You have existing relationships within the nonprofit sector, particularly with senior fundraising and marketing leaders, or you have successfully built a meaningful professional network from the ground up.
  • You understand the dual nature of this role. You care deeply about the quality of the experience, but you also recognize that the work must support measurable membership and commercial outcomes.
  • You bring strong business development instincts. You think in terms of pipelines, follow up consistently, and remain accountable to your goals.
  • You understand that the fortune is in the follow-up and know how to use HubSpot or a similar CRM to manage prospects, track activity, and maintain accurate reporting.
  • You are a thoughtful and persuasive written and verbal communicator who knows how to connect with a senior executive audience.
  • You are comfortable using LinkedIn Sales Navigator and other prospecting tools to research and engage prospective members.
  • You stay informed about nonprofit fundraising and marketing trends and can confidently participate in conversations about topics such as iROI, donor lifetime value, CRM hygiene, acquisition costs, and attribution.
  • You exercise sound judgment and know how to build relationships without making interactions feel forced or transactional.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working within a nonprofit organization, ideally in development, fundraising, or marketing.
  • Experience hosting or supporting an executive peer group, mastermind, or invitation-only event series, such as YPO, Vistage, Chief, EO Forum, or a similar organization.
  • An established presence within professional fundraising communities such as AFP, NTEN, Bridge, Nonprofit Tech for Good, or Fundraising.AI.

Location

This is a fully remote, part-time position open to candidates located in the United States. Because The Giving Table currently operates in New York City, Washington, D.C., and Atlanta, preference will be given to candidates based in New York City or Washington, D.C.

Travel to select Giving Table dinners, events, and gatherings will be required.

Compensation

This part-time role offers an annual salary of $50,000–$70,000, plus a performance-based bonus tied to membership growth and downstream commercial outcomes. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and existing industry relationships.

Delve Deeper is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diversity enriches the workplace, and we are committed to growing our team with the most talented and passionate people from every community. Delve Deeper strives to create a culture of unity and respect. To that end, we have a zero-tolerance policy for behavior that promotes harassment, hate, or discrimination of any kind. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals. If you require assistance during the application process due to a disability.

Salary: $50,000 - $70,000

This role is ideal for researchers who want to see their work directly impact product capabilities while maintaining a focus on cutting-edge innovation.

You are driven by curiosity and technical discovery. You see research as a systematic process of exploration and validation, not just theoretical work.   • Experience training and evaluating ML models on real datasets
  • Understanding of model evaluation metrics, experimental design, and statistical validation
  • Familiarity with data preprocessing, augmentation, and management for ML workflows
  • Experience presenting research findings to technical audiences

Nice To Have

  • Expertise in real-time inference, model optimization, or efficient architectures
  • Experience with self-supervised learning, few-shot learning, or foundation models

  • Contributions to open-source ML projects or released research code

  • Background in edge computing, on-device ML, or resource-constrained environments

Forward Deployed Solutions Engineer (Early Career)

Location: Canada (Remote or Hybrid)

Employment Type: Full-Time

Build technology that solves real business problems.

At Hiveway, we believe software should make work simpler—not more complicated.

We build payment and revenue automation solutions that help organizations modernize how they collect payments, connect business systems, and eliminate manual processes.

We're looking for curious, ambitious engineers at the beginning of their careers who want more than a traditional software development role.

If you're excited by solving real customer problems, building production software, and learning directly from experienced engineers while working with enterprise customers, we'd love to meet you.

What is a Forward Deployed Solutions Engineer?

A Forward Deployed Solutions Engineer (FDSE) combines software engineering, solution architecture, and customer problem-solving into one role.

Instead of working only from a product backlog, you'll work alongside customers to understand how their business operates, identify technical challenges, and help build solutions that create measurable business impact.

You'll learn how software, payments, APIs, data, finance, and business operations come together to solve real-world problems.

No two projects are exactly the same—which means you'll constantly learn, grow, and be challenged.

What You'll Do

Working alongside experienced engineers and mentors, you'll help:

  • Build production software and customer solutions
  • Design and develop API integrations
  • Connect payment, CRM, ERP, and accounting systems
  • Automate manual business processes
  • Design data workflows and reconciliation logic
  • Investigate and resolve production issues
  • Participate in customer discovery sessions
  • Translate business challenges into technical solutions
  • Improve existing platform capabilities
  • Document and share technical best practices

You'll work across Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and directly with customers.

What You'll Learn

This role is designed to accelerate your career.

During your first year you'll gain experience in:

  • Software engineering best practices
  • Solution architecture
  • API design and integrations
  • Payment technologies
  • Cloud applications
  • Production operations
  • Customer discovery
  • Enterprise software implementation
  • Systems thinking
  • Technical communication

You'll receive mentorship while taking on meaningful responsibility from day one.

What We're Looking For

You don't need to know everything.

We're looking for people with strong fundamentals and an eagerness to learn.

You may be a great fit if you:

  • Love solving difficult problems
  • Enjoy learning new technologies
  • Ask thoughtful questions
  • Communicate clearly
  • Take ownership of your work
  • Like understanding how businesses operate
  • Enjoy collaborating with both technical and non-technical people
  • Are curious about APIs, integrations, automation, or cloud software
  • Want to see your work used by real customers

Minimum Qualifications

We're interested in candidates who are completing or have recently completed a degree or diploma in areas such as:

  • Computer Science
  • Software Engineering
  • Computer Engineering
  • Systems Engineering
  • Electrical Engineering
  • Mathematics
  • Data Science
  • Information Systems
  • Physics
  • Mechatronics

Equivalent technical experience is also welcome.

You should also have:

  • Experience programming in at least one modern language
  • Understanding of software engineering fundamentals
  • Familiarity with Git
  • Basic understanding of APIs, databases, or web applications
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent communication skills

Programming languages may include:

  • TypeScript / JavaScript
  • Python
  • Java
  • C#
  • Go
  • C++
  • Or another modern language

Bonus Points

We're especially interested if you've:

  • Completed internships or co-op placements
  • Built applications people actually use
  • Created personal or open-source projects
  • Participated in hackathons
  • Worked with APIs
  • Built full-stack applications
  • Worked at a startup
  • Automated repetitive work
  • Built something outside the classroom

We care much more about what you've built than where you've built it.

How We Work

At Hiveway we believe:

Start with the problem.

Understand the customer before designing the solution.

Build for production.

Reliable software beats clever software.

Stay curious.

The best engineers are always learning.

Own outcomes.

We take responsibility for solving problems—not just completing tasks.

Keep improving.

Every customer teaches us something that makes our platform better.

Your First 90 Days

You'll receive structured onboarding, mentorship, and regular feedback.

During your first three months you'll:

  • Learn Hiveway's platform and development environment
  • Shadow customer meetings
  • Contribute production code
  • Build your first integration or workflow
  • Participate in architecture discussions
  • Learn our engineering standards
  • Work with experienced engineers on customer implementations

As your confidence grows, so will your ownership.

What Success Looks Like

Successful engineers at Hiveway:

  • Ask great questions
  • Learn quickly
  • Build reliable software
  • Communicate effectively
  • Solve customer problems
  • Take ownership
  • Continuously improve
  • Help others succeed

Why Join Hiveway?

Large companies often give new graduates a very small piece of a very large system.

At Hiveway, you'll see the entire picture.

You'll learn directly from experienced engineers, work with enterprise customers, contribute to production systems, and influence how our platform evolves.

You'll gain experience across engineering, product, customer solutions, and business operations while helping solve meaningful problems for growing organizations.

If you want a role where your work matters from the beginning, Hiveway is the place to build your career.

Position Overview

We are seeking a senior, hands-on CJA Product Modernization Consultant or Engineer to deliver a defined workstream within an enterprise Adobe Analytics-to-Customer Journey Analytics transformation.

Working with a Level 1 CJA Product Modernization Architect, this individual will translate modernization strategy into schemas, datasets, identity configurations, CJA connections, data views, metrics, reports, integrations, validation processes, and implementation deliverables.

This is not a general Adobe modernization role. Direct, hands-on CJA experience is required; Adobe Analytics experience without CJA implementation experience is not sufficient.

  • Lead detailed analytics requirements and process-discovery sessions.

  • Build or migrate Analysis Workspace projects and reporting components.
  • Execute data reconciliation and validation across Adobe Analytics, AEP, source systems, and CJA.
  • Support parallel reporting, testing, defect resolution, cutover, and production readiness.
  • Document schemas, datasets, mappings, metrics, test plans, and deployment procedures.
  • Identify and escalate data-quality, identity, integration, performance, privacy, and governance concerns.
  • Support training, documentation, governance, and business adoption.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of digital analytics, analytics implementation, data engineering, Adobe consulting, martech, or related experience.
  • Direct, hands-on Adobe Customer Journey Analytics implementation experience.
  • Strong Adobe Analytics and Adobe Experience Platform experience.
  • Experience supporting or delivering an Adobe Analytics-to-CJA migration.
  • At least one official Adobe certification is required; the exact certification must be clearly listed on the resume.
  • Hands-on experience with several of the following: XDM schemas, datasets, ingestion, identity, CJA connections, data views, metrics, filters, calculated metrics, attribution, sessionization, Analysis Workspace, and validation.
  • Experience translating business measurement requirements into functional or technical solutions.
  • Experience with testing, validation, documentation, deployment, and production readiness.

Preferred Qualifications

· Multiple Adobe certifications.

  • Experience combining digital and non-digital data for cross-channel reporting.

What Success Looks Like

  • Legacy requirements are translated into an improved CJA model.

  • Stakeholder Communication: Partner cross-functionally to translate complex analytics into clear, actionable business recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Requirements

jobs.title: Open Call - Soil Carbon Field Tech (Contract - Central US based)
jobs.excerpt: Overview Yard Stick is looking for a number of Soil Carbon Field Technicians to help us fight climate change with soil.
jobs.description:
Overview
Yard Stick is looking for a number of Soil Carbon Field Technicians to help us fight climate change with soil. This role is an essential part of Yard Stick’s primary on-the-ground operations, deploying our novel soil carbon measurement technology as well as traditional soil testing methodology on fields across the US. This is a contracted seasonal/part-time 1099 position. We are a small company with big ambitions, and therefore we need people who are highly entrepreneurial, reliable, comfortable with travel, and committed to working towards solving climate change.
Location flexible, and significant cross-country travel is required. Hourly pay (including pay for time spent travel), and travel expenses will be paid for.
About Yard Stick PBC
Yard Stick is a remote-first, seed-stage company, with founders based in Boston and Oakland. We are on a mission to reverse climate change with agriculture. Scientists and farmers alike know that climate-friendly agricultural practices have the potential to remove atmospheric CO2 at gigaton/year scale. When these practices are adopted, more carbon is stored in soils, improving soil health and fighting climate change. But significant measurement challenges have held soil carbon efforts back - until now.
By reducing the cost of soil carbon measurement by 90%+, Yard Stick will dramatically expand the opportunities for evidence-based regenerative practices to simultaneously improve ecosystem health, increase farmer income, and combat climate change.
Current soil carbon measurement technologies are slow, expensive, and cumbersome, relying on conventional soil cores and labs to quantify carbon stocks. In contrast, Yard Stick is fast and cheap - without sacrificing accuracy. As a testament to our technology’s potential, alongside our scientific collaborators, we were awarded a $3.6M grant from the DOE ARPA-E Smartfarm as well as other highly competitive grant programs which reward technical merit like NSF SBIR. For more background, check out some coverage in TechCrunch or Treehugger.
We've also raised money from top climate VCs, including Breakthrough Energy Ventures (Bill Gates' climate fund), Lowercarbon Capital (Chris and Crystal Sacca's climate fund), MCJ Collective, and others. Details of the financing aren’t announced in a press release or article, because that can feel a bit cart before the horse, but we're happy to share more detail about our funding when we chat.
About The Role
This Soil Carbon Tech role is critical to the success and rollout of Yard Stick’s offerings and works in-field across the country and a variety of project types to meet our R+D and client goals. The Yard Stick team and our client base is spread across the country, but our current focus is primarily in the Midwest. We’re growing quickly, and this position will be an essential role with significant responsibility.
You will be primarily responsible for testing our hardware and software in fields across the US to help us evaluate and improve our technology’s accuracy, durability, and usability. You will be leading projects geared towards calibrating our technology, as well as collecting measurements to quantify stocks on client lands using a variety of different methodologies.
You’ll provide feedback on hardware and software tools alike, as Yard Stick has innovative offerings in both domains. Obviously, when stuff breaks, you’ll document why and help us brainstorm ways to improve.
Yard Stick’s offerings combine a large number of disparate disciplines, including highly technical hardware, a web app which manages carbon measurement and GIS data, and ML pipelines which connect the two. This person ultimately will work cross-disciplinarily along with our hardware, software, soil science, and business teams alike to maximize the pace of Yard Stick’s R&D and therefore climate impact, so the ability to communicate clearly to a wide range of people is a must.
We need someone who can handle rigorous field work with efficiency and exceptional precision. The ideal candidate for this role is comfortable traveling, working outdoors, handling a wide array of equipment, and working in a team off 2-6 people through projects that can include rapid schedule changes, long days, and inclement weather.
Currently, Yard Stick is focused on proof of concept of our in situ spectral probe. Generating high-quality, publishable data requires excellent field operations. In parallel, we’re also creating our commercial offerings. This role will be crucial in carrying out both streams of work.

Qualifications - Must Have

  • Some combination of education and/or experience in natural sciences, agriculture, conservation, soil science, natural resource management or another related field of study. We don’t require formal education, but one way or another, you have the experience that’ll make you comfortable on farms and around producers, and are no stranger to having your hands in the dirt.
  • Extensive experience and comfort with physical field work. Experience working with your hands out in the field is key to this role. You don’t flinch at the idea of 8 hours in the sun moving from customer farm to farm, sometimes for two weeks straight.
  • Comfort with field tools, technologies and strategies. Our offerings use technologies like GPS, ATVs, and mobile app-based sample inventory tracking systems. You can drive an ATV, or you’re not afraid to learn. You use mechanical tools comfortably. Note: Yard Stick will provide a vehicle if you don’t have one for this role, or will generously reimburse if you do.
  • Attention to detail and commitment to craft. When you take a 30 cm soil core, it’s 30 cm. You care deeply about the details. You take written instructions well, triple-check your work by nature, and will follow an SOP to the letter. You are proud to do your work very well.
  • Strong personal independence and entrepreneurial autonomy. If you can’t get your boss on the phone, you figure it out. You assess the situation, consider solutions, make a plan, and execute, even if your closest coworker is 100 miles away.
  • Comfort with extended travel. Projects can often be in remote areas of the country -- spending a week or two at a time away from home is essential to this role.
  • Personal enthusiasm and comfort in agricultural contexts. You care about farming or ranching. The idea of helping activate agriculture to fight against climate change excites you. It matters to you that you’re working on a problem of existential significance.
  • Ability to share product feedback to improve systems. When you’re asked for feedback, you pay attention and communicate observations clearly, especially in writing. You document things carefully and are curious when using new products or technologies.
  • Existing permanent authorization to work in the United States.

Qualifications - Nice To Have

  • Personal, durable enthusiasm for the challenge of climate change.
  • Awareness of current issues in carbon markets - particularly carbon removal. You’ve heard of offsets/credits and some of the attendant criticism of low-quality projects of the past and present. You’ve got some basic knowledge about how carbon markets work, and you’ve heard about how carbon removal is a new, exciting, and controversial approach to climate challenges.
  • There will be a significant portion of the year that we’re not sampling, and we’re interested in other skills you can bring to the team! Specifically if you have any of the following, we’d love to hear about it: GIS or other mapping software; vehicle and equipment maintenance; equipment + logistics management; agricultural sales or similar; agronomy; data science, etc.

Compensation and Other Details

  • $30-40/hr to start, with travel expenses (including time) paid. Performance raise after a set number of projects have been completed.
  • Remote first, Midwest/Plains preferred (NE/KS/CO/IA)
Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
Yard Stick’s impact goals go well beyond climate science (although our #1 core value is Climate Impact). Why? Our company operates primarily in the US agricultural sector, which is predicated on centuries of mass land theft and disenfranchisement of Native and Black people. This harm continues today. If we’re going to work in this sector, we need to actively work to make it better.
Consistent with our core value of “Pursue Justice,” we speak up about these issues, and we support emerging solutions and relevant policy efforts such as and . We also publicly highlight the risk of further racial discrimination in emerging agricultural legislation like the Growing Climate Solutions Act.
Regarding hiring and culture, we work to create a work environment where everyone feels confident sharing their ideas, problem-solving happens openly and collaboratively, and mistake-making is welcomed. We also standardize our interview process and questions to reduce “likeability” bias, benchmark salaries against industry databases to reduce negotiation, and utilize tools like the Gender Decoder (this one is feminine-coded, fwiw). Climate change is arguably the most complex challenge ever faced by humanity - we need all of humanity activated to fight back, and that motivates us to build a diverse team.

About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

About the Role:

Sezzle is currently seeking a Data Analyst to help drive business outcomes through analytics. This role presents an opportunity to work in a fast-paced, high growth environment while partnering with stakeholders across the organization to identify opportunities, measure performance, and improve operational efficiency.

You will collaborate with teams across Product, Engineering, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Support, Legal, and People Operations to define key metrics, build reporting solutions, and deliver actionable analysis. Responsibilities include writing SQL queries, developing dashboards, performing exploratory analyses, and contributing Python-based analytics workflows that support scalable decision-making across the business.

What You'll Do:

  • Work closely with business teams to understand their priorities and analytics needs
  • Create sophisticated analyses and reporting to provide insights at scale that support strategic initiatives and empower data-informed decision-making
  • Visualize and articulate analytics results to make it easy for stakeholders to interpret and take actions
  • Help stakeholders identify new opportunities through data analysis
  • Create, monitor, review, and analyze reports and dashboards, take initiative to fix issues that arise and conduct root cause analyses
  • Utilize modern AI tools, including LLMs, copilots, and workflow automation platforms, to enhance analytical productivity and develop scalable solutions to business problems

What We Look for:

  • Degree in statistics, math, actuarial science, economics, data science, computer science or related quantitative discipline
  • Master’s degree or 3+ years of professional experience working with data, which can include: complex dataset creation, reporting, profiling, and machine learning
  • Expert in using SQL to extract data and create actionable data sets
  • Experience with Python for data processing and analytics
  • Ability to complete analyses with minimal guidance
  • Experience with data visualization tools such as Redash, Tableau, Looker or Power BI
  • Comfortable making impactful decisions in a fast-paced and sometimes ambiguous environment, able to pivot quickly to new priorities
  • Excellent problem-solving skills
  • Strong business judgment and communication skills
  • Fluent in English

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Graduate degree in a quantitative discipline
  • Experience optimizing operational and financial performance
  • Experience in payments, financial services, banking, fintech, BNPL

The Tech You’ll Work With:

  • Python
  • Redshift, PostgreSQL
  • Data build tool (dbt)
  • AWS, G Suite, Mac
  • Coding agents Claude, ChatGPT

Interview Process:

  • Application submitted (you are here)
  • Wonderlic test (30-40 min)
  • Coding assessment (~1.5 hours)
  • Interview with recruiters (30 min)
  • Verbal case study interview. Share how you approach new problems. A “How would you…” conversation.
  • Verbal behavioral interview. Share your problem-solving experience. A “Tell me about a time when you…” conversation.
  • Offer!

About You:

  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome:

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

jobs.description:
The role:

You will be the operating second to the CISO and own the bank-entity scope of Mercury's 2LOD Information Security program. You'll be the person who keeps the program examiner-ready by default: coherent policy architecture, evidenced controls, a credible gap-remediation track record, and a tested incident response program with documented exercise history.

This is not a research or strategy role. It is a build-and-defend role. You will sit across the table from OCC examiners, FFIEC IT audit teams, our Chief Risk Officer, and the board's risk committee, and you will be expected to answer for every line in our policies and every status in our control inventory.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC

What you'll own:

  • Bank-entity 2LOD InfoSec program. Governance, policy, risk, and oversight scoped to the chartered bank.
  • Examiner posture. OCC, FFIEC, FDIC and FRB examiner inquiries; ownership of the examiner-ready narrative; coordination of the evidence.
  • FFIEC control remediation. Lead remediation of identified FFIEC IT control deficiencies to charter readiness ahead of the OCC pre-opening examination
  • Policy architecture. Carry the bank-scoped policy stack (Policy / Standard / Procedure), including ratification cycles, MRCC memos, and board approvals.
  • BC/DR. Partner with the Chief Risk Officer on bank continuity, resilience, and recovery, including tabletop exercises and full-scale drills.
  • Audit and assurance. Manage relationships with internal audit (3LOD) and external assessors (SOC 2, FFIEC CAT, regulator-led IT examinations).
  • Third-party risk. Ensure TPRM evidence holds up to bank-grade scrutiny for critical service providers and material outsourcing arrangements.
  • Team development. Coach and grow the GRC sub-team; run a recurring training cadence; build the bench depth a national bank requires.

What we need:

  • 8+ years in Information Security, with 3+ years inside a regulated bank, trust bank, or de novo bank charter effort. Mercury is a startup chartering a national bank — this experience is non-negotiable.
  • Deep FFIEC and OCC fluency. You have deep working knowledge of the FFIEC CAT, the FFIEC IT Examination Handbook, BSA/AML IT supervisory expectations, and the OCC Heightened Standards.
  • Direct examiner-facing experience. You have defended a control to an OCC, FDIC, or Federal Reserve examiner. You know what good evidence looks like before it gets challenged.
  • Policy and standards craft. You can draft a board-ratifiable policy and the supporting standards stack that operationalizes intent, not just satisfies a checklist.
  • Operating discipline. You run cadences, write status that survives executive review, and maintain currency of controls, evidence, and risk registers.
  • 2LOD instinct. You understand the three-lines-of-defense model and have served in the oversight role.

What we'd love:

  • Prior Deputy CISO or equivalent senior 2LOD role at a national bank, trust bank, or large credit union.
  • Charter or de novo bank experience — if you've stood one up before, that is a meaningful advantage here.
  • Strong technical baseline, you don't need to be an engineer, but you should be able to challenge an architecture review and read an incident timeline credibly.
  • CISSP, CISM, or CRISC

What success looks like:

  • At 30 days - You have developed working knowledge of Mercury’s FFIEC IT control inventory and roadmap, every in-flight policy draft, and met one-on-one with the GRC team. You can speak to the top ten risks in the bank-entity program by name.
  • At 90 days - You are running the weekly bank charter status cadence, leading examiner-readiness reviews, and personally accountable for at least three priority program tracks. The CISO is briefing the board and the MRCC with material you authored.
  • At one year - The charter timeline is on track. The bank-entity Information Security program sustains supervisory-grade standards as a standing posture. You are the executive other functions consult to determine whether a security risk is material.

Why this role:

We are building a security program designed to protect Mercury and enable the business. Chartering a national bank does not change that philosophy. It does mean we need a Deputy who can hold the bar to OCC standards without losing the operating tempo that has defined Mercury since inception.

As our Senior Payroll Operations Analyst, you will own end-to-end pay run execution across all company entities, serving as the function's primary processor and systems administrator. This role is built for a practitioner who leads with data, operates with precision, and holds the line on accuracy and compliance at every stage of the pay cycle.

You will work cross-functionally with HR, Finance, People Operations, and Legal to operationalize processes that are built to scale, and serve as a trusted resource for employees seeking timely, accurate answers to pay-related questions. As the business grows, so does your ownership. This is a role designed to expand with the function and the team.

Key Responsibilities:


Payroll Processing (40%)

  • Execute end-to-end biweekly payroll as the lead Preparer for all on-cycle and off-cycle runs
  • Prepare and validate payroll inputs: new hires, terminations, bonuses, retroactive adjustments, and one-time payments

  • Deliver completed audit packages to Reviewer per the Preparer > Reviewer > Approver control model

Tax & Withholding Administration (20%)

  • Validate paycheck-level taxation accuracy across multi-state jurisdictions
  • Monitor withholding account activity and flag discrepancies for remediation
  • Process garnishments, levies, and involuntary deductions within established timelines
  • Support quarterly and year-end tax reconciliation and filing validation
  • Research multi-state tax requirements, wage and hour regulations, and withholding rules as needed
  • Maintain compliance tracker for active tax jurisdictions and filing deadlines
Equity Administration (10%)

  • Process equity transactions in the payroll system and validate against the equity management system
  • Ensure accurate supplemental withholding on equity-based compensation events
  • Maintain equity-to-payroll audit logs and support year-end equity reconciliation
  • Partner with Stock Administration and Finance on equity event coordination
Systems Administration & Analytics (15%)

  • Monitor and validate payroll system settings, workflow automations, and configuration setups
  • Identify configuration errors, recommend improvements, and document resolution steps
  • Build ad hoc reports for internal and external requests from Finance, People, and Legal partners
  • Track accuracy and efficiency metrics against established KPIs
  • Support GL reconciliation and payroll-to-finance reporting deliverables
Data Integrity & Records Management (10%)

  • Maintain payroll master data including employee pay records, configuration logs, and period-over-period audit trails
  • Perform routine audits of pay elements, earnings/deductions setups, and tax profiles
  • Maintain organized drive folders and records in accordance with retention policy
  • Ensure SOPs, checklists, and playbooks remain current and audit-ready
Employee Support & Cross-Functional Collaboration (5%)

  • Serve as Tier I and Tier II escalation point for employee payroll inquiries
  • Provide accurate guidance on pay, taxes, deductions, equity events, and processes
  • Collaborate with HR, Finance, People Operations, and Legal on input submissions and policy questions
  • Represent payroll operations in cross-functional meetings and audit reviews

Qualifications:


Required:

  • 5+ years of payroll operations experience with direct processing ownership in a multi-state environment
  • Advanced technical proficiency with HRIS and payroll systems
  • Strong analytical and data validation skills with demonstrated accuracy in high-volume environments
  • Working knowledge of wage and hour law, pay computation, and multi-state tax compliance
  • Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills; exposure to macros or query tools a plus
  • Excellent attention to detail, confidentiality, and time management in a fast-paced environment
Preferred:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred; FPC or CPP certification is a plus
  • Prior experience with Rippling or comparable enterprise payroll platform
  • Equity transaction processing experience and payroll tax administration for equity-based compensation
  • Experience working in healthcare, startups, or high-growth multi-entity environments

Description

🤓 TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We've been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners — people with no prior tech background — through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.

We're looking for the person who brings a Forward Deployed Engineering curriculum to life for students: you would be part of a team of senior authors who help create the content for the course. The best person for this is someone who has actually gone into client environments and carried AI deployments to production, has opinions about what a sound deployment looks like, and can tell an experienced engineer why their approach is wrong.

Your audience: Working production engineers, not career changers, with six to fifteen years in, mostly backend, with senior and staff engineers and the occasional engineering manager. They've shipped real software for years and are moving deliberately into forward-deployed AI work; some are already interviewing for FDE roles while they study. What they're missing is agentic systems and the client-facing half of delivery.

Format: asynchronous, estimated 20 hrs/week.

Please submit all resumes or CVs in English.

What you will do

  • Design and build the projects students work on end to end — scope, learning goals, technical infrastructure, environments, and supporting databases or datasets.
  • Write clear submission guidelines and assessment criteria (rubrics) that reviewers can apply consistently.
  • Work closely with Learning Experience Designers to make projects and lessons educationally sound and engaging: refining wording, pacing, and difficulty calibration across the course.
  • Research, evaluate, and sign off on technical solutions and tooling so the curriculum stays current and relevant to what employers actually use.
  • Contribute to sales and marketing enablement — training commercial teams on what the course covers and what graduates can do.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of professional engineering experience, currently working at senior level or above (Senior/Lead/Staff Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Architect, or technical lead on customer-facing delivery).
  • Has personally owned deployments end-to-end in real client or enterprise environments – first call through production go-live and adoption.
  • Practical experience with databases and the infrastructure needed to run student projects (cloud environments, containers, version control, CI where relevant).
  • Ability to break complex technical work into scoped, assessable tasks at a defined difficulty level.
  • Strong written communication in English — you'll produce a lot of instructional text and it needs to be unambiguous.
  • Comfort collaborating cross-functionally with instructional design, and explaining technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience mentoring, teaching, tutoring, or reviewing others' code.

Preferred experience:

  • Prior EdTech or rubric/assessment design experience.

What we can offer you

  • Fully remote work.
  • A digital office: we use modern tools (Notion, Slack, Zoom) to keep collaboration smooth.
  • Professional trust and autonomy: no micromanaging.
  • A diverse, international, close-knit team excited to work with you!

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Our Enterprise Customer Success Managers pick up where our Implementation team leaves off, working closely with our top customers to understand their fleet and unique challenges, advising on how to customize Samsara for their needs, and becoming their long-term partner.

Your role will be cross-functional in nature, working alongside and connecting Sales, Support, Sales Engineering, and Product, enabling you to experience multiple aspects of a hyper-growth company from within.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except Alaska, Austin Metro, Boulder Metro, California, Chicago Metro, Connecticut, Dallas Metro, Denver Metro, Houston Metro, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, Seattle Metro, and Washington, D.C.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the Public Sector: You’ll be working with cities, states, school districts, and universities that help run our world. You'll work with them to help them operate more efficiently, safely, and drive citizen value through their services.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will:

  • Be on the front-lines and ensure our customers increase the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of their operations with our IoT platform
  • Compose joint success plans with customers, outlining their objectives, metrics, timelines, and effectively removing any barriers to achieving business value
  • Orchestrate executive business reviews with our customers’ decision makers and our executive leadership where we look back at past successes and align on upcoming goals
  • Conduct workshops with customers to understand their current operations and recommend workflow changes to get the most out of their Samsara products
  • Deeply understand the Samsara platform’s capabilities and explain them to businesses of all types - field services, utilities, long-haul transportation, school buses, and many more
  • Serve as a mentor to the wider Customer Success and Support teams
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 3+ years of experience in a senior Customer Success, account management, or strategic consulting role. Enterprise SaaS experience preferred
  • This is a demanding position with high internal visibility, that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence
  • Experience supporting or working with technical products
  • Solutions-oriented with strong problem solving skills
  • Proven track record of building trust and communicating effectively with a wide variety of stakeholders: executives, Product and Engineering leadership, day-to-day users of our software
  • Passion for going above and beyond the call of duty, taking initiative, and thriving in a fast-paced, change-heavy environment
  • Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues
  • Bachelor’s degree from a 4-year institution

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Strong bias for action, the ability to think big, with insistence on high standards
  • Experience serving and supporting large-scale solutions for Public Sector organizations
  • Thrives in an unstructured, fast-paced, and change-heavy environment

Annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below and depends on your city of residence. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary
$97,877.50—$131,600 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

Join DayOne – Shaping the Future of Data Infrastructure

DayOne is a global leader in the development and operation of high-performance data centers. As one of the fastest-growing companies in the industry, we’ve built a robust presence across Asia and Europe — and we’re just getting started.

As we expand into new international markets, we’re looking for talented, driven individuals to join us on this exciting journey. This is more than a job — it’s an opportunity to be a key contributor to our dynamic team and help shape the future of global data infrastructure.

If you're passionate about innovation, technology, and growth, we invite you to be part of DayOne’s next chapter.

Position Summary

The Senior Director, AI Infrastructure Architecture is DayOne’s senior technical authority for the architecture of AI-ready DC platforms. The role defines how compute, high-performance network fabrics, storage, fibre, power, cooling and physical deployment systems integrate into scalable AI POD and AI Factory solutions.

Building on the Network Systems Advisor remit, this permanent leadership role combines customer and OEM engagement, reference architecture, ecosystem development and organizational capability building. It enables DayOne to make credible customer commitments and develop repeatable platforms for high-density AI training and inference workloads, while partnering with Design and Operations teams that retain accountability for facility delivery and operation.

Key Accountabilities

  • AI platform architecture: Define end-to-end reference architectures for modular AI PODs and AI Factory deployments, integrating GPU/accelerator compute, scale-up and scale-out fabrics, high-performance storage, external connectivity and management networks.

  • Network and optical architecture: Set topology, performance, resilience, routing, oversubscription, addressing, structured cabling and optical design principles across InfiniBand, Ethernet/RoCE and emerging ultra-high-speed technologies.

  • Compute and storage integration: Define infrastructure requirements for GPU clusters, host platforms, NVMe-oF and parallel storage, ensuring data paths and capacity models support training and inference performance.

  • Physical infrastructure integration: Partner with facility engineering to align rack layouts, fibre pathways, containment, power density, liquid cooling, controls, maintainability and commissioning with AI system requirements.

  • Customer and OEM engagement: Lead technical discovery and architecture workshops with customers, GPU and server OEMs, network vendors, storage providers and integration partners; translate requirements into deployable specifications.

  • Pre-contract technical assurance: Support sales and investment decisions with solution options, assumptions, indicative configurations, delivery constraints, cost drivers and technical risk assessments.

  • Standards and playbooks: Create governed reference designs, interface standards, requirements templates, deployment patterns and acceptance criteria that can be reused across markets and customer programmes.

  • Partner ecosystem: Shape preferred partner frameworks and technical evaluation criteria for compute, storage, networking, optics, fibre and system integration suppliers.

  • Capability and operating model: Assess organizational capability, define specialist roles and build the architecture, network engineering, fibre delivery and validation capabilities required to scale.

  • Technology roadmap: Track and evaluate emerging AI infrastructure technologies, balancing innovation with interoperability, supply chain, lifecycle, security and operational readiness.

  • Technical governance: Chair AI architecture reviews, maintain architecture decision records and provide expert escalation for cross-layer performance, interoperability and deployment risk.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Network Engineering or a related technical discipline; advanced degree advantageous.

  • Typically 15+ years in data centre network, high-performance computing, cloud infrastructure or AI infrastructure architecture, with senior technical leadership responsibility.

  • Deep expertise in high-radix Clos fabrics, InfiniBand and Ethernet/RoCE architectures, routing, optics, structured fibre and high-density physical deployment.

  • Strong understanding of GPU cluster architecture, high-performance storage, workload data flows and the power/cooling implications of AI platforms.

  • Proven experience defining reference architectures and converting customer/OEM requirements into buildable deployment specifications.

  • Track record of vendor evaluation, partner ecosystem development and influencing executive investment decisions.

Success Measures

  • Approved, reusable AI POD and AI Factory reference architectures with clear performance and interface requirements.

  • Reduced solution cycle time and technical risk in AI-related pursuits and deployments.

  • Validated integration across compute, storage, network, fibre, power and cooling domains.

  • Strong OEM/customer confidence and improved quality of pre-contract technical commitments.

  • Qualified partner ecosystem and measurable improvements in deployment readiness and repeatability.

  • Development of sustainable internal architecture, fibre engineering and validation capability.

We encourage you to explore Have Fun and Is Motion Gaming Back?, as they offer a deeper look into our culture, values, and explain how our approach to motion gaming differs from previous generations.

To protect yourself from recruitment scams, please note that Nex communicates through official company emails ending in @nex.inc. If you receive a suspicious email or message, please do not respond and report it immediately to us.

Location: Remote
Annual salary:USD 190,000– USD 215,000
Type: Full-time
Reports to: General Counsel

About the Role

We're looking for an experienced commercial attorney to lead legal support for Nex's content and partnerships ecosystem - the agreements and relationships that bring games, experiences, and brand collaborations onto the Nex Playground platform. You will be the primary legal partner to our Content, Partnerships, and Business Development teams, negotiating content and IP licensing deals, developer and publishing agreements, and strategic partnerships that grow our content catalog and platform reach. You'll also provide secondary support on our commercial vendor, retail/distribution, and hardware supply chain agreements as needed, in partnership with the GC and outside counsel.

This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to build the playbook for a growing platform business, not just execute one that already exists.

What You'll Do

Content & Developer Agreements

  • Draft, review, and negotiate developer and publishing agreements for third-party studios and content creators building games and experiences for the Nex Playground platform, including revenue share, IP ownership, quality/certification requirements, and platform terms.
  • Structure and negotiate Play Pass content licensing and distribution agreements, balancing catalog growth with sustainable economics and IP protection.

Brand & Strategic Partnerships

  • Lead negotiation of brand and content licensing agreements with entertainment and children's media partners, including royalty structures, approval rights, marketing commitments, and IP/trademark compliance obligations.
  • Serve as the go-to legal partner to Business Development and Partnerships teams on strategic collaborations, co-marketing arrangements, and platform integrations, functioning as a strategic advisor embedded in partnership planning rather than a late-stage reviewer.
  • Independently lead complex, multi-party negotiations involving revenue-sharing arrangements, joint go-to-market plans, and cross-promotional commitments.

Commercial, Vendor & Hardware Support (Secondary)

  • Support retail, distribution, vendor, and marketing agreements as needed, partnering with Legal Operations on templates and process.
  • Provide secondary review and negotiation support on manufacturing, supply chain, and OEM/ODM agreements alongside the GC and outside counsel.
  • Partner with Product Counsel to identify commercial, product liability, regulatory, and privacy issues arising from any transaction you touch. Flag privacy/COPPA-relevant terms to Product Counsel, who owns Nex's privacy program and day-to-day privacy advisory work - you are not expected to advise on these substantively yourself.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Process

  • Build trusted relationships with [Content, Partnerships, Business Development, Product, and Marketing] - you'll be known as the attorney teams want in the room when a deal is taking shape, not just when paper needs signing.
  • Partner with Legal Operations on intake triage, template design, and CLM workflow design for content, developer, and partnership agreement types.
  • Manage and coordinate outside counsel on specialized or high-stakes IP, regulatory, or hardware/supply chain matters, with Legal Operations administering the underlying vendor relationship and spend.
  • Use AI-powered legal tools to accelerate contract review, drafting, and analysis, and help identify opportunities to further integrate AI into the team's workflows.
  • Contribute to Nex's broader legal function build-out over the next 18 months - templates, policies, and training - as one of the company's early in-house attorneys.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Hold a J.D. and active bar membership in good standing (California or another U.S. state, as applicable).
  • Have 7-10+ years of combined law firm and in-house experience, including meaningful time supporting a content/media partnerships business.
  • Have direct experience negotiating publishing/content licensing deals; experience with brand/entertainment IP licensing is a strong plus.
  • Understand partnership economics: how revenue share and attribution work, and how to structure incentives that align interests between Nex and its content and brand partners.
  • Are comfortable operating in an entrepreneurial environment with little existing precedent. You are proactive, independent, and energized by building rather than maintaining.
  • Communicate with clarity and business judgment, tailoring advice to enable responsible, fast-moving growth, and are comfortable presenting partnership strategy to business leaders.
  • Demonstrate sound judgment in ambiguous or fast-changing situations, and can distinguish real risk from theoretical risk.
  • Are willing and able to flex into commercial, vendor, or hardware-adjacent agreements when the business needs it, even though that's not the core of the role.
  • Bring genuine curiosity about AI tools and how they're reshaping commercial legal practice.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at a gaming or consumer content/media company. Experience negotiating with entertainment studios, media brands, or children's content licensors.
  • Working knowledge of children's privacy frameworks (e.g., COPPA) or international data privacy regimes as applied in a commercial/platform context.
  • Some exposure to hardware, manufacturing, or supply chain agreements - helpful for the secondary scope of this role, though not the primary focus.
  • Familiarity with CLM systems (Spotdraft, Ironclad, or similar) from a heavy end-user or template-owner perspective.

What Success Looks Like

  • [Content, Partnerships, and Business Development] teams have a legal partner they trust to move deals forward quickly and with confidence.
  • Developer, content, and brand partner agreements are negotiated efficiently, with clear risk framing and business-enabling solutions.
  • Brand and licensing partnerships are structured to protect Nex's IP and reputation while still closing quickly.
  • Privacy and platform compliance issues are surfaced early and routed to Product Counsel, not resolved after the fact.
  • Templates and negotiation playbooks scale with the business so Legal doesn't become a bottleneck as Nex's content and partnership ecosystem grows.

We Offer

  • Competitive compensation package.
  • Flexible working hours and vacation policy.
  • Product-driven culture that treasures talents and individual growth.
  • Front-row seat and hands-on experience with cutting edge technologies in the evolving gaming field

Job Title: Medical Billing & Reconciliation Specialist

Position Type: Part-Time

Work Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM Bermuda Time
Work Days: Sunday to Thursday
Salary: $5–$6 per hour, depending on experience
Workplace: Remote

About the Client & Role

Our client is an occupational healthcare organization in Bermuda managing employee health services, medical appointments, fit-to-work documentation, billing information, and coordination with physicians and vendors.

They are seeking a highly detail-oriented and independent Medical Billing & Reconciliation Specialist to support backend healthcare operations, with a strong initial focus on billing reconciliation, data management, documentation, and EMR administration. Over the first 60–90 days, the role may gradually expand into more patient-facing responsibilities, including scheduling, reminders, and follow-ups.

The ideal candidate has healthcare billing or accounting experience, strong Excel skills, prior EMR experience, and the ability to identify discrepancies and resolve administrative issues without requiring constant supervision.

Responsibilities

Billing Reconciliation & Data Accuracy

  • Reconcile billing information, co-payments, and supporting records.
  • Review billing data for accuracy, identify discrepancies, and coordinate necessary corrections.
  • Maintain accurate financial and administrative documentation.

EMR, Excel & Administrative Support

  • Update Excel spreadsheets and Prognosis EMR using information collected from physician offices and other EMR systems.
  • Support the transition of workflows and data from Excel to Prognosis.
  • Learn client systems thoroughly and identify opportunities to improve administrative workflows.

Scheduling & Patient Follow-Up

  • Schedule occupational health appointments and maintain accurate patient schedules.
  • Send appointment reminders and follow up on confirmations or outstanding scheduling needs.

Medical Records & Documentation

  • Collect and document information following physician appointments.
  • Gather blood work, hearing and vision screening results, and other required occupational health records.
  • Obtain and follow up on physician fit-to-work notes and ensure required documentation is complete.

Communication & Coordination

  • Communicate with supervisors, physicians, vendors, and patients regarding appointments, documentation, and outstanding requirements.
  • Maintain consistent follow-up and build professional rapport with patients while adapting to different communication styles.

Requirements

Required Experience & Skills

  • Experience with medical billing, accounting, reconciliation, or healthcare operations.
  • Previous experience using an EMR/EHR system.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel and experience managing detailed spreadsheets.
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when handling billing, financial information, and healthcare data.
  • Ability to work independently without constant supervision or follow-up.
  • Professional and assertive communication skills.
  • Comfortable communicating with patients from varied backgrounds and handling direct or informal communication professionally.
  • Willingness and ability to learn Prognosis EMR quickly and become highly proficient with the platform.

Software & Systems

  • Prognosis EMR
  • OptoMantra
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft SharePoint
  • Microsoft 365 / Office 365

Basic Requirements

  • Must speak and write English clearly and professionally.
  • Must have relevant work experience.
  • Must be able to provide an NBI Clearance and/or Local Police Clearance before onboarding (mandatory).
  • Must be available to attend video meetings with camera on when required.

Technical Requirements

  • Computer: Reliable laptop or desktop computer.
  • Internet: Stable high-speed internet connection (minimum 25 Mbps).
  • Audio: Noise-canceling headset.
  • Video: Working webcam for virtual meetings.
  • Workspace: Quiet and professional work environment.

Benefits

  • Dedicated HR & Contractor Support Team: Access to world-class support for questions, guidance, contract matters, and client communication.
  • Premium VPN Access (Optional): A secure VPN license can be provided upon request to enhance privacy and security for client-related tasks.
  • HIPAA & Cybersecurity Training + Certification (Provided): Access to our internal HIPAA compliance training, cybersecurity modules, and certification to help you confidently handle PHI for U.S. healthcare clients.
  • Top 1% VA Performance Training: Access to our proprietary training on communication, client management, productivity systems, and best practices to help you become a top-performing VA and increase long-term client retention.
  • Client-Approved U.S. Holidays: Contractors may take U.S. holidays off according to the client’s needs and schedule.
  • Client-Approved Paid or Unpaid Time Off: Time off may be granted by your client. Paid time off is optional and only if offered by the client.
  • Access to Tools & Resources: Templates, workflow guides, productivity tools, and client-specific SOP support to help you perform at your best.
  • Optional Performance-Based Incentives: Some clients may offer bonuses, incentives, or increased hours based on your performance.

These are optional resources and client-approved allowances available to you as an independent contractor. Any resources, training, or allowances listed are optional contractor perks and not employee benefits.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The SEO Associate supports the day-to-day execution of SEO campaigns across our dental client base. Working closely with U.S.-based specialists, you'll handle tracking and analytics setup for new accounts, keyword research, on-page optimization, technical fixes, and local SEO — the hands-on, on-site work that gets campaigns launched correctly and keeps them moving.
This is a role for someone who wants to build real SEO depth. You'll work across a wide range of client sites, learn from senior specialists daily, and see the direct impact of your work in the data.
This is a fully remote role supporting a U.S.-based team. Clear, proactive written communication matters as much as technical skill.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Tracking & Analytics Setup

Set up Google Analytics 4 for new accounts — create the property and data stream, and configure conversion events for form submissions, calls, chat, and booking.
Install and configure Google Tag Manager, and confirm there is exactly one container and one property on the site.
Set up Google Search Console — verify ownership, submit the XML sitemap, request indexing, and link the property to GA4.
Verify every installation before sign-off using Tag Assistant and GA4 real-time — confirming the correct IDs are firing and events are recording.
Set up client dashboards and integrate data sources in Agency Analytics.
Troubleshooting
Diagnose tracking issues — tags not firing, events not recording, duplicate containers or properties, and conversions that stop reporting.
Investigate sudden drops in traffic or conversions to determine whether the cause is a tracking failure or a genuine performance change.
Resolve access and permission issues across Google properties, and coordinate with clients or internal teams to get what's needed.
Keyword Research & On-Page Optimization
Research and select target keywords for client websites, accounting for search intent, volume, and competitive difficulty.
Map keywords to the right pages and flag gaps where a target keyword has no page to rank.
Optimize website pages — meta titles and descriptions, header structure, and image alt text.
Build internal links that connect service pages, location pages, and existing pages in a way that reflects the site's architecture.
Technical SEO
Identify and fix basic technical issues including broken links, missing tags, duplicate content, and missing alt attributes.
Run and interpret site crawls, and flag anything beyond your scope to the assigned specialist.
Monitor indexation and crawl health in Search Console, and raise issues early.
Coordinate with web developers to implement changes that require developer access.
Local SEO
Support Google Business Profile optimization — profile fields, services, service descriptions, categories, and photos.
Maintain listing accuracy across directories and resolve sync errors or duplicate listings.
Verify business name, address, and phone details are consistent everywhere they appear.
Performance Reporting
Track keyword rankings, organic traffic, and conversions across your assigned accounts.
Share concise, regular performance updates with the U.S. team — what moved, what didn't, and what you think is behind it.
Flag meaningful declines early rather than waiting for a scheduled review.
Collaboration & Additional Responsibilities
Communicate clearly and proactively with U.S.-based team members and project leads.
Coordinate with web developers and designers to get changes implemented.
Escalate anything requiring a strategic judgment call to the assigned specialist rather than guessing.
Contribute to cross-team projects, process improvements, and new initiatives as assigned.
Take on new responsibilities and special projects as business needs evolve, with opportunities to learn and grow.
CORE COMPETENCIES:
Communication: Writes clearly, concisely, and proactively in English. Shares updates before being asked and raises blockers early.
Attention to Detail: Catches a missing meta description, a broken internal link, or a tag that isn't firing before it affects performance or data.
Technical Aptitude: Comfortable setting up and verifying tracking, reading a crawl report, and working in a CMS without hand-holding.
Process Discipline: Follows documented processes consistently, and flags when a process doesn't fit the situation.
Organization & Time Management: Handles work across multiple client accounts and deadlines without dropping threads.
SEO Fundamentals: Solid working knowledge of on-page, off-page, and technical SEO — enough to work independently on defined tasks.
Problem-Solving: Diagnoses the actual cause rather than treating the symptom, and focuses on practical, actionable solutions.
Initiative: Takes ownership of assigned accounts and looks for improvements nobody asked for.
PERSONALITY MUSTS:
Our perfect fit is someone who is a problem solver who understands the difference between “yes, and…” and “yes, but…”. You should have a hungry, scrappy personality with a positive attitude and aims to deliver. Working in the client service industry can mean going the extra mile, and we need someone who is always willing to rise to the occasion for our clients and puts forward beautiful work that exceeds client expectations. Someone who is detailed and organized, driven and displays vigor and comes ready to play every day. Confidence, self-discipline, and a congenial, curious mind are things we love and admire.
The ideal SEO Associate is curious, detail-oriented, and genuinely interested in why rankings move. You verify rather than assume — you'd rather spend the extra ten minutes confirming a tag is firing than trust that it is. You're comfortable working independently in a remote role, you communicate without needing to be chased, and you'd rather ask a clarifying question than ship something you weren't sure about. A positive attitude, hunger to grow, and willingness to take ownership are a must.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Excellent written and verbal communication in English — clear, concise, and proactive.
Hands-on experience setting up Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager, including configuring conversion events.
Experience with Google Search Console setup and verification.
Working knowledge of SEO best practices across on-page, off-page, and technical.
Experience with Ahrefs and/or SEMrush.
Experience with Agency Analytics.
Experience with Webflow or a comparable CMS.
Reliable high-speed internet connection.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow documented processes.
BONUS POINTS FOR APPLICANTS WITH:

Google Business Profile and local SEO experience

or comparable project management tooling
